articles.chapeau: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' is here for console gamers, but remains one of the most-anticipated video games of all time on PC.
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto VI is available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles at launch (it will also be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming , with limits).
GTA 6 has no confirmed PC release date. Given Rockstar's history with PC ports, we originally thought gamers were in for a long wait.
An October 2026 report from gaming business media site Gamesbeat reveals a potential PC launch in early 2027, which is sooner than we expected.
Grand Theft Auto VI arrived on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on Nov. 19, 2026, but PC players will have to wait a while longer. Rockstar has confirmed that the game will not be available for PC gamers at launch, and no PC version has been officially announced yet.
Despite that, we recently got some good news: GamesBeat reports that GTA 6 will get a PC release sometime in Q1 of 2027. GamesBeat has a good track record with unannounced news like this. According to their reporting, the GTA 6 PC release window was confirmed by industry sources familiar with Rockstar's plans. They spoke with the outlet under the condition of anonymity.
Rockstar and Take-Two haven't given an official reason for skipping PC at launch, but a few factors are typically cited when publishers stagger releases this way.
Console hardware is standardized, which tends to make optimization more straightforward than building for the huge range of PC configurations. Some industry data has also indicated that consoles generate higher per-unit revenue, giving publishers an incentive to front-load console sales.
A more cynical take is that Take-Two could just be double-dipping, hoping fans who can't wait for the PC launch will buy the console first, then buy the PC version later. A PC Gamer poll found that 39 percent of respondents said they're fine waiting for a port rather than needing it on day one, suggesting a meaningful share of the PC audience isn't treating the delay as a dealbreaker.
However, there could be another, less financially motivated reason for all of this.
Speaking to YouTuber KiwiTalkz , former Rockstar producer John Ricchio explained that building for consoles first and scaling up to PC is technically easier than the reverse, since consoles have fixed, predictable hardware. According to IGN , Ricchio said it's simpler to start with tighter constraints and add polish later than to build a PC-first game and then try to trim it down to fit console limitations.
Without an official release date, gamers have had to speculate on the most likely launch window for a GTA 6 PC version.
If you look at several past Rockstar games, you can see that there's typically a significant amount of time between the console launch and the PC port.
Grand Theft Auto 4 was released in April 2008 and didn't reach PC's until December. Grand Theft Auto V was released in Sept. 2013, and its PC counterpart was released 19 months later in April 2015. Red Dead Redemption 2 arrived on PC roughly a year after its console release.
The one exception was Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy – The Definitive Edition , which launched simultaneously across platforms in 2021. Based on that track record, a GTA 6 PC port, if it follows the usual pattern, could be a year or more away.
A report from The Verge claimed that Xbox would have exclusive rights to stream GTA 6 via its cloud gaming service at launch, a claim that was recently confirmed. The report noted that PC gamers would be able to play GTA 6 on day one , despite Rockstar's lack of news about a potential release window for a PC port. Unfortunately, Xbox Gaming's Chief Strategy Officer, Matthew Ball, shot down this report. Ball wrote on his personal X account that The Verge's coverage led to some "misreporting."
Again, the game will be available to play on Xbox consoles via Xbox Cloud Gaming, but that service faces strict monthly limits, which will make it difficult to play through the game in a timely fashion.
Fortunately, a GamesBeat report suggests gamers may not have to wait a full year for a PC release, though it remains unconfirmed.

articles.t: Cyberleek pushes GTA 6 PC efforts forward with the Xbox build .exe release
articles.chapeau: While the official launch date for GTA 6 on PC remains uncertain, the leaked Xbox build might help bridge the gap for eager fans.
articles.txt:
Cyberleek has released the missing executable for the leaked 209GB Grand Theft Auto 6 Xbox build ahead of schedule, giving modders and reverse-engineering groups another piece of the puzzle as they work toward getting the game running on PC. The release follows a cryptocurrency fundraising campaign tied to a $15 million meme coin market cap target, which was later reduced to $6 million.
The original Xbox files began circulating on November 19 , but the package lacked an essential .exe file, preventing anyone from attempting to launch the build. Cyberleek had initially promised to distribute the missing executable once tonce the November 23rd deadline passed,. However, the file started appearing on piracy websites just before the countdown expired .
Although its arrival is a significant development for people examining the leaked build, it does not mean GTA VI is suddenly playable on Windows. Cyberleek previously predicted that developers could produce a bootable PC version within a week, potentially through emulation or by adapting the game to run natively.
Neither approach is straightforward, as developers still face substantial technical challenges, including shader translation , memory management, and adapting the game's software environment to Windows. One such open-source compatibility layer project, VIctory , aims to translate GPU shaders and recreate console-specific features so GTA VI 's Xbox x86-64 code can run directly on Windows. Anyone struggling to keep track of the numerous projects can now follow their progress in one place on PortWatchVI .
Cyberleek also included a text document alongside the executable, reiterating the motivations behind the leak and the cryptocurrency campaign. According to the message, previous GTA 6 gameplay leaks deliberately avoided major story spoilers because the intention was not to ruin the experience for players. Instead, Cyberleek directed criticism toward Rockstar Games and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, particularly over the delayed arrival of a dedicated PC version.
For now, the executable represents another development in the ongoing effort to examine the leaked Xbox build, rather than an immediate route to playing GTA 6 on PC. Whether the wider project delivers anything beyond the current leaks remains to be seen.

articles.t: GTA 6's Staggering Sales Still Might Never Catch GTA 5
articles.chapeau: The new game's day-one sales defy belief, but so does its big brother's long-term record
articles.txt:
On Friday, Rockstar Games' parent company Take-Two Interactive announced sales figures for Grand Theft Auto 6 that are so dizzying, I'm still processing them. They have clearly shattered preorder records for video games and launch sales — in fact, total sales – for just about any form of entertainment.
Take-Two said that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies during its pre-release period, and that through the end of launch day on Nov. 19, it had racked up $3.79 billion in revenue.
Comparisons are fun to make, but apt ones don't really exist. On its day of launch, GTA 6 had made twice as much money as Taylor Swift's entire Eras tour , and more than any film has ever made across a full theatrical run. Alinea Analytics reckons that by the end of the weekend the numbers were up to 44.9 million copies sold and a round $4 billion in revenue. It took GTA 6 one day to eclipse the lifetime sales figures of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild .
Here's a more meaningful comparison: Grand Theft Auto 5 took three days to hit $1 billion in sales. GTA 6 's launch is four times bigger than its predecessor's. It will definitely crush GTA 5 's lifetime record, right? Well… not necessarily.
As amazing as GTA 6 's sales are, it has a long, long way to go to catch up with its big brother. GTA 5 is the second-best selling game of all time behind Minecraft (or third-best, depending on how you account for sales of Tetris ). It has sold a staggering 235 million copies to date, more than two and a half times as many as the next game in the all-time ranking, Rockstar's own Red Dead Redemption 2 .
When it comes to long-tail, long-term sales, GTA 5 is in a different class entirely — a class of two, alongside Minecraft . It's not a given that GTA 6 will necessarily be able to join this class. A few things have to fall into place.
Image: Rockstar Games Rockstar has yet to confirm a PC version of the game, for starters, though one is expected in 2027. That will unlock a whole new audience for GTA 6 , especially globally, and supercharge its sales again.
Rockstar has also yet to confirm that it will create a GTA 6 version of GTA Online . GTA 5 's scrappy multiplayer mode became a live-service behemoth that has driven a huge proportion of those 235 million sales, and that financially sustained Rockstar through the extremely long and expensive developments of Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 6 . Analysts also seem confident in predicting GTA 6 's online mode will arrive in 2027, although I think a degree of skepticism is warranted on that part.
Rockstar hasn't said one word publicly about GTA 6 Online for good reason. Migrating online gaming audiences, who’ve invested massive amounts of time and money in their accounts, from one game to a sequel is notoriously difficult. It's why there was never a World of Warcraft 2 , for example, and there are vanishingly few examples of it being done successfully ( Destiny 2 being, perhaps, the exception that proves the rule).
Image: Rockstar Games This is not to say that Rockstar won't do it, but the studio will need to be extremely careful and consider its strategy. Will it lock the new online mode behind a full purchase of GTA 6 , as it initially did with its predecessor? Sell it separately and/or bundle it in a GTA Plus subscription, as it now does for GTA Online ? Or maybe even go free-to-play? These approaches all have their advantages and drawbacks when it comes to tempting GTA Online players to upgrade and maximizing the new online game's revenue, but only one of them is going to help GTA 6 sell as many copies as GTA 5 .
There's a final but important asterisk to consider with respect to GTA 5 's astonishing sales. It has been released across three console generations, and a lot of those purchases will be duplicates or even triplicates (which is especially true for GTA Online players).
In other words, the sales figures are likely flattering to the maximum size of the GTA audience; I don't think there are 235 million GTA players out there. It's going to be challenging for GTA 6 to meet that number unless it, too, spans three generations. I hope we won't be waiting until late in the PlayStation 7's life for GTA 7 , but you never know with Rockstar.
One thing's for sure: Rockstar's only real competition is itself. GTA 6 has had the biggest launch imaginable. Can it also go the distance?

articles.chapeau: Stealing cars just like you did back in 2001 on the PS2
articles.txt:
Obviously, you need to steal cars in Grand Theft Auto 6 ; it’s in the name of the game. But you might as well get something out of it beyond just new wheels and some money, so how about scoring a trophy along the way?
The Bravado Banshee is a nice ride that you get a mission to steal in GTA 6’s third chapter, via a character named Randy. You could luck out and find a Banshee on the street, but if you want the Capital Offense trophy, you can kill two birds with one stone by hitting up the Sunrise Premium Autos showroom in Southside. You’ll find it between Vice City International Airport and Peacock Bay, next to an Illegals Good Store.
Note that you can’t do this before you do Randy’s mission “Clonin’ Keys, Makin’ Gs.” Why? The Bravado Banshee, like a lot of expensive cars in the game, requires a key cloner , and Randy is the person who gives you one as part of that mission. After he’s added the app to your phone, you can head to Sunrise Premium Autos and walk back to the showroom where a shiny blue Bravado Banshee is just sitting there.
Clone the key via the same method you would use to slim-jim a car door, and then step on in. The next part is how you get the Capital Offense trophy: Drive the car straight through the glass window and then gun it before the police get there. The trophy should pop immediately.
The trophy itself is a reference to the easiest and most reliable way to get a Banshee in Grand Theft Auto 3 , where you would just visit a car showroom in the south part of the map, sit in a Banshee in the showroom, and then drive it through the glass window. The similarity to that setup here in GTA 6 seems to be a pretty direct reference to the now-25-year-old PS2 title.
You can either give the Banshee to Randy for that mission or get it repainted and registered for yourself. And you can return later to this same spot and get another Banshee! Regardless of what you choose, you’re a bit richer and a bit further along in your progress toward a platinum trophy or a mythic achievement. Not bad for an afternoon’s work.

articles.t: "Ça nous paraissait tellement évident de mettre The Weeknd dessus" : Justice dévoile les coulisses de la BO de "GTA 6"
articles.chapeau: INTERVIEW FUN RADIO - Justice dévoile les coulisses de sa collaboration avec The Weeknd sur la BO de "GTA VI", entre évidence artistique, hésitation initiale et clin d'oeil caché dans le jeu.
articles.txt:
Une évidence… que Justice a d'abord voulu repousser. Dans L'After Fun Radio , le duo raconte comment The Weeknd a rejoint la bande originale de GTA VI . Dès la composition, sa voix s'impose : "À la minute où on a écrit l'instrumental, on pensait à Abel. Ça nous paraissait tellement évident de mettre The Weeknd dessus." Mais les musiciens attendent plusieurs mois avant de le contacter. Leur réserve ? "Il faut se méfier parfois de ce qui est trop évident." L'intuition finit par l'emporter. Amateur de Grand Theft Auto , le chanteur répond avec enthousiasme et se met aussitôt au travail. " Il nous a dit ok, c'est cool, j'enregistre un truc cette nuit ." Un jour et demi plus tard, Justice reçoit une version déjà très proche du morceau final. Cette collaboration pourrait pourtant échapper à de nombreux joueurs. Intégré au mode histoire, le titre occupe une place que le duo préfère garder secrète. "C'est presque un easter egg", glisse Justice : une surprise que ceux qui délaissent les missions pour explorer librement le jeu risquent de manquer. Une rencontre évidente, mais presque cachée.

articles.chapeau: Nothing monumental, but every little bit helps.
articles.txt:
By now, anyone reading this has probably gotten themselves a PS5 or Xbox and played at least a handful of hours of Grand Theft Auto VI after it launched last week. Next time you go to play the game on your console of choice, there will likely be a patch you have to download.
On Monday, Rockstar released the first official post-launch update for GTA 6 . It's not a hugely seismic patch by any means, as it largely addresses a handful of in-game glitches that range from minor to major. Since GTA 6 is not a multiplayer game, you might be able to play it without downloading the patch, but based on the patch notes, you will probably want to wait for it to install first.
According to Rockstar's update notes, the first GTA 6 patch is intended to fix seven common bugs players had encountered in the first few days after launch. Here are all the things Rockstar said it fixed on Monday:
An issue that caused weather to not change for extended periods of time
"Several issues" that caused in-game phone calls, including ones that push the story forward, to not trigger on time
An issue that caused partner characters to not hand bags of contraband to the player
As you can see, these range from minor irritations to nearly game-breaking glitches. Phone calls not triggering properly is especially bad, as they regularly unlock new story missions. Obviously, not being able to lose a wanted level would also be a pretty big bummer.

articles.t: "On n'était pas sûrs d'être forcément les bonnes personnes" : comment Justice a accepté le défi de "GTA 6"
articles.chapeau: INTERVIEW FUN RADIO - Justice raconte sur Fun Radio comment le duo a composé la musique de "Grand Theft Auto VI".
articles.txt:
Avant de composer pour GTA VI , Justice a d'abord hésité. Flatté par la proposition de Rockstar, le duo voulait mesurer l'ampleur du projet. "On n'était pas sûrs d'être forcément les bonnes personnes pour faire ça", confient les musiciens au micro de Fun Radio, depuis le studio Motorbass. Leur lien avec l'éditeur remonte à GTA IV , où figurait déjà l'un de leurs morceaux.
Pour cette nouvelle collaboration, c'est le même interlocuteur qui les a recontactés. Un passionné, expliquent-ils, qui connaissait leur discographie "par cœur" et s'intéressait aussi à des titres moins connus, pas seulement à leurs tubes. Une approche qui a convaincu Justice qu'il ne s'agissait pas de refaire ce qu'ils avaient déjà produit, mais bien d'inventer une musique pensée pour l'univers du jeu.
Pour comprendre les attentes de Rockstar, Justice passe une semaine dans ses studios à New York. Au programme : regarder le jeu huit heures par jour et échanger avec les équipes. Le duo veut vérifier qu'il peut apporter quelque chose au projet, sans faire perdre de temps à ses interlocuteurs. "Après une semaine à discuter, on s'est dit ok, faisons-le." L'accord marque le début d'un travail qui s'étirera sur plusieurs années. Une durée que l'un des musiciens résume avec humour : " Quand j'ai commencé, j'avais un enfant. Quand on a fini, j'en avais trois ."
Justice précise avoir travaillé sur la musique du mode histoire, plus particulièrement sa partie urbaine. Une mission différente de l'ajout de morceaux aux radios du jeu : il s'agit ici d'écrire une musique qui accompagne l'action et les émotions. Dans le respect du secret entretenu par Rockstar, le duo échange régulièrement avec les superviseurs musicaux. Les pistes sont confrontées aux images, testées, retravaillées. " Beaucoup d'aller-retour, beaucoup d'ajustement ", résument les musiciens. Disco, métal, funk, pop ou électronique : leur palette devient un outil au service du récit. "Il fallait toujours que ce soit justifié à l'image." Rockstar ne recherchait d'ailleurs pas spécialement leur dimension French touch ou club, mais aussi leurs influences rock et disco.
Même logique pour les invités : l'amitié ou le prestige d'un nom ne suffisent pas. Chaque participation doit répondre à une question : " Est-ce que ça apporte quelque chose au jeu ou pas ? " Cette exigence s'accompagne d'un pari : accepter que certains joueurs n'entendent jamais une partie du travail. Ceux qui délaissent les missions pour explorer librement l'univers peuvent passer à côté de morceaux, y compris celui avec The Weeknd, décrit comme "presque un easter egg". Pour Justice, c'est aussi la singularité de cette première expérience de composition pour un jeu vidéo : une musique dont la découverte dépend du parcours de chacun.

Une chanson de Sylvie Vartan , incluse dans le jeu vidéo phénomène GTA 6 et adaptée du tube What a feeling a vu ses écoutes bondir plus de quarante ans après sa sortie, suscitant la «surprise totale» de la star de la chanson française. «Ça a été une surprise totale, donc c'est absolument génial de savoir qu'une chanson que je chantais il y a quelques années a voyagé un peu partout et va encore renaître» , a confié à l'AFP la star de 82 ans, interprète de nombreux tubes dont «La plus belle pour aller danser» (1964).
Céline Dion, la superstar qui revient de loin PODCAST - Écoutez le club Le Figaro Culture avec Jean-Christophe Buisson TV ce soir : retrouver notre sélection du jour Grand Theft Auto 6 , que plus de 39 millions de joueurs uniques ont lancé depuis sa sortie jeudi, est tout aussi apprécié pour son scénario et le réalisme de ses personnages que pour sa musique omniprésente. Outre la bande-son composée par le duo électro français Justice , les joueurs peuvent naviguer sur la vingtaine de radios et parmi les quelque 800 morceaux disponibles dans GTA 6 .
C'est ainsi que Danse ta vie tourne sur Kaleidoscope FM, l'une des radios de Vice City où se déroule le jeu. Sortie en 1983, il s'agit d'une reprise en français de What a Feeling d'Irene Cara, tube emblématique du film Flashdance . «Les écoutes du titre ont bondi de plus de 2500% dans le monde par rapport à la semaine précédente, avec un compteur qui s'affole dès le 20 novembre, au lendemain de la sortie du jeu vidéo» , a relevé la plateforme audio Spotify.
Le titre est plébiscité en France mais aussi aux États-Unis, en Allemagne et au Canada, précise le géant du streaming. «C'était ma chanson d'ouverture au Palais des congrès (de Paris) : je cherchais une chanson sur laquelle je pouvais danser et qui pouvait avoir le rythme nécessaire pour ouvrir le spectacle. Ce sont des bons souvenirs qui reviennent !» , a retracé l'artiste aux plus de 40 millions de disques vendus.
Parmi les pionnières du rock en France, puis figure des Yéyés avant d'évoluer vers la pop, Sylvie Vartan avait déjà connu un succès viral en 2025 avec «La Maritza» . Ce titre de 1968 sur son enfance en Bulgarie, avait été utilisé par des milliers d'utilisateurs sur les réseaux sociaux. La chanteuse assure ne pas avoir su à l'avance que ce morceau allait figurer dans «GTA VI» , un jeu qu'elle qualifie d' «absolument incroyable» , tout en confiant n'y avoir encore jamais joué. «Je vais m'y mettre, peut-être ! Même si je n'ai pas trop le temps» , sourit-elle.

GTA 6 accusé d’être « woke » : la colère des masculinistes
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 accusé de « wokisme » : Lucia et Jason cristallisent la colère masculiniste. Analyse des représentations et des enjeux économiques mondiaux.
articles.txt:
Avec 3,79 milliards de dollars de ventes mondiales dès sa première journée de commercialisation, Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) signe le plus grand lancement de l’histoire du divertissement, selon son éditeur. Mais le jeu vidéo est aussi devenu la cible d’influenceurs masculinistes qui accusent Rockstar Games d’avoir cédé au « wokisme ». En cause : une héroïne indépendante, Lucia Caminos, et un personnage masculin, Jason Duval, qui témoigne de l’affection à sa compagne. Une polémique révélatrice de la diffusion des discours masculinistes dans la culture populaire, de leur économie et de leur conception des rapports entre les femmes et les hommes.
Dans un jeu vidéo où les joueurs peuvent incarner des criminels, commettre des braquages et affronter les forces de l’ordre, offrir des fleurs à sa compagne serait-il devenu un acte subversif ? Depuis la sortie mondiale de GTA 6, le 19 novembre 2026, plusieurs influenceurs de la manosphère américaine dénoncent les choix narratifs de Rockstar Games, accusant le studio d’avoir sacrifié l’identité masculine de la franchise au profit du féminisme et de l’inclusivité.
Lancée en 1997, la série Grand Theft Auto a longtemps suscité des controverses en raison de sa violence, de ses représentations sexualisées des femmes et de la possibilité de recourir à la prostitution. Près de trente ans plus tard, la polémique s’est déplacée : c’est désormais la représentation d’une masculinité moins dominatrice qui provoque l’indignation d’une partie de ses détracteurs.
Treize ans après la sortie de GTA V, Rockstar Games a choisi de placer au cœur de son nouvel opus un couple de criminels évoluant dans un État américain fictif inspiré de la Floride. Lucia Caminos, ancienne détenue d’origine latino-américaine, et Jason Duval, ancien militaire, doivent coopérer pour survivre dans un environnement particulièrement violent.
Lucia marque une évolution importante dans l’histoire des principaux épisodes de la franchise. Alors que les femmes ont souvent occupé des rôles secondaires ou hypersexualisés dans GTA, elle dispose de ses propres ambitions, prend des décisions et participe pleinement à l’action.
Avant même la commercialisation du jeu, le magazine américain Wired avait documenté la multiplication des accusations de « wokisme » visant Rockstar Games. Certains internautes dénonçaient notamment la place accordée aux femmes et aux minorités, ainsi que les changements supposés dans les orientations éditoriales du studio.
Depuis la sortie du jeu, c’est également la relation entre les deux protagonistes qui concentre les critiques. Jason peut offrir des fleurs à Lucia, organiser des soirées en amoureux, l’accompagner dans certaines activités quotidiennes ou participer à l’aménagement de leur logement.
La disparition de la possibilité de recourir à la prostitution, présente dans la franchise depuis GTA III en 2001, alimente également les accusations de censure. Certains détracteurs reprochent au scénario de privilégier la fidélité du personnage masculin.
GTA 6 conserve pourtant les éléments caractéristiques de la série : violence explicite, criminalité, nudité et univers destiné aux adultes. Ce n’est donc pas tant la disparition de la transgression qui est en cause que l’évolution de certaines représentations des rapports entre les sexes.
Le streamer américain Asmongold, de son vrai nom Zack Hoyt, a qualifié GTA 6 de « cuck simulator », une expression particulièrement révélatrice du vocabulaire de la manosphère. Dérivé de l’anglais cuckold , signifiant littéralement « cocu », le terme est employé pour disqualifier les hommes considérés comme soumis aux femmes ou insuffisamment virils.
Myron Gaines, figure du podcast masculiniste Fresh & Fit , est allé plus loin en contestant la place même des femmes dans l’univers du jeu vidéo. Dans une intervention du 21 novembre, il a défendu l’idée que certaines sphères, dont les jeux vidéo, devraient rester réservées aux hommes. Ces déclarations ont été recensées par Media Matters for America dans une publication du 24 novembre.
Jason présente pourtant de nombreux attributs traditionnellement associés à la virilité : il est musclé, ancien militaire et capable de s’imposer dans un environnement criminel. Mais sa puissance physique ne semble pas suffisante aux yeux de certains détracteurs dès lors qu’il accorde de l’importance aux besoins et aux décisions de sa compagne.

articles.chapeau: Sylvie Vartan n'avait jamais joué à un jeu vidéo. La voilà pourtant au cœur de Vice City : « Danse ta vie », diffusé dans GTA 6, a vu ses écoutes bondir de plus de 2.500% sur Spotify
articles.txt:
Personne ne l’avait vu venir, et surtout pas elle. À 82 ans, Sylvie Vartan voit un morceau de 1983, « Danse ta vie », repartir à l’assaut des classements grâce à « GTA 6 ». Le jeu vidéo de Rockstar, lancé jeudi, a déjà séduit plus de 39 millions de joueurs uniques, plébiscité autant pour son scénario et le réalisme de ses personnages que pour sa bande-son omniprésente.
Les chiffres donnent le vertige. Selon Spotify , les écoutes du titre ont bondi de plus de 2.500 % dans le monde par rapport à la semaine précédente, avec un compteur qui s’affole dès le 20 novembre, au lendemain de la sortie du jeu. Le morceau est surtout plébiscité en France, mais aussi aux États-Unis , en Allemagne et au Canada : un raz-de-marée pour une chanson vieille de plus de quarante ans.
Dans GTA 6, la chanson tourne sur Kaleidoscope FM , l’une des vingt radios de Vice City, la ville où se déroule l’action. Elle y côtoie quelque 800 morceaux, ainsi que la bande-son composée par le duo électro français Justice. Sortie en 1983, « Danse ta vie » est une reprise en français de « What a Feeling » d’Irene Cara, tube emblématique du film « Flashdance ».
Principale intéressée, la chanteuse ne cache pas sa stupeur : « Ça a été une surprise totale, donc c’est absolument génial de savoir qu’une chanson que je chantais il y a quelques années a voyagé un peu partout et va encore renaître ». L’interprète de « La plus belle pour aller danser » (1964), aux plus de 40 millions de disques vendus, assure n’avoir rien su à l’avance de cette présence dans le jeu.
Ce titre fut sa chanson d’ouverture au Palais des congrès de Paris : « Je cherchais une chanson sur laquelle je pouvais danser […]. Ce sont des bons souvenirs qui reviennent ! »
Déjà virale en 2025 avec « La Maritza », la pionnière du rock français n’a pourtant jamais touché à la manette. Elle compte s’y mettre, « peut-être », même si elle n’a « pas trop le temps ».

The One Thing to Know About Jason and Lucia Before You Play Too Much GTA 6
articles.chapeau: Stronger together
articles.txt:
Even after clearing Grand Theft Auto 6 ’s long story, I keep finding myself drawn back to Leonida. That’s thanks in large part to Jason and Lucia, a pair of charismatic protagonists that I genuinely enjoy spending time with. While you can treat them as independent characters and take them out on solo adventures, GTA 6 shines brightest when you travel around Leonida as a pair. In fact, you’re bound to miss a whole lot if you aren’t letting Jason and Lucia enjoy a date from time to time.
While playing as one character in GTA 6 , you have the option to invite your partner to hang out with you. (This feature unlocks partway through Chapter 2 of the story.) If you’re playing as Jason, for instance, you could text Lucia and ask if she wants to hang out, prompting her to drive to your location. You can coordinate crimes this way too; if you find a bank you want to rob, you can ping Jason and tell him to meet Lucia at the spot to pull off the job together. There are a lot of benefits to working together, as heists will become easier and you’ll be able to ask your partner to run off and fence any goods you grab.
But keeping Jason and Lucia together has some less obvious benefits, too. When the two explore together, they’ll occasionally break out into natural conversations. One time while driving through Lummox County listening to a country radio station, Lucia talked about how she thought the genre was a joke growing up. A little odd couple exchange ensued, where Jason talked about how much he loves country music. Later, upon finding a stray bicycle, Lucia told Jason about the time she tried to ride a bike as a kid and crashed into an ice cream truck.
Image: Rockstar Games There are even entire running gags that you’ll only hear while playing together. One recurring bit involves Lucia constantly answering spam robocalls and gradually losing her cool over them. That culminates in her giving the AI voice a firm thrashing, while Jason chuckles from the sidelines. Those bits of contextual chatter help make Jason and Lucia feel like an authentic couple rather than voiceless pawns to be moved around.
More importantly, crucial story details can come out of those moments. One time while exploring a swamp in search of Skunk Ape effigies (weird game!), Jason and Lucia broke out into a conversation about their family dynamics. It started when Jason mentioned Lucia’s mother doesn’t like him very much. After a bit of unconvincing denial, Lucia admitted that there’s truth to Jason’s anxiety: Lucia lied to her mother, saying that Jason essentially walked out on her and their child. That revelation triggered a conversation where Lucia recalled a moment where Jason once told her he didn’t want children, which is why she initially didn’t tell Jason about their son. It’s an important moment that gives depth to Jason and Lucia’s history and fills in some questions about why Tommy was kept secret for so long.
So, if you’ve been exploring Leonida solo for most of your GTA 6 playthrough, make sure to invite your partner to hang out regularly. You’ll miss some of the best human moments in the game if you do, and you’ll understand each character so much more by listening to their chatter. And, of course, you’ll also be able to send Jason off with a bag full of cocaine if you don’t want to trek back to Vice City to sell it.

articles.chapeau: Hackers are trying to get GTA 6 running on PC, Mac, and Linux without the help of Rockstar following a major game file leak
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto 6 ' s official release seemed like the end for apparent hacker Cyberleek , who raised millions of dollars in cryptocurrency by sharing unauthorized video of the open-world game ahead of launch. Rather than fading into obscurity, Cyberleek upped the ante by releasing an apparent build of GTA 6 onto the internet. And now, hackers, vibe coders, and programming enthusiasts are rushing to try and make GTA 6 playable on PC before Rockstar does.
Those following along might recall Cyberleek as the hacker who spent weeks provoking Rockstar Games . In addition to supplying the internet with leaked footage of the unfinished version of the game, Cyberleek also critiqued Rockstar and parent company Take-Two Interactive's business practices . The leaker claimed they objected to GTA 6 's digital-only release as well as its pre-order bonuses. Cyberleek encouraged Rockstar and Take-Two to change course by dangling the possibility of sharing the files they were using to play the game to the public.
This suggestion was particularly shocking since Rockstar has not made the game available outside of console platforms. The game also doesn't exist on a disc, meaning that players don't have access to the game files. Without such data, players can't peek under the hood of the game — and they definitely could not tinker with it in unintended ways, like forcing the characters to appear without clothes in the overworld.
Cyberleek's motives seemed questionable, especially since the hacker gated the release of the alleged files behind monetary milestones. One of those early milestones included nude gameplay featuring the game's co-protagonist Lucia which successfully rallied fans to donate money. Once Cyberleek shared the footage, however, the hacker lost their leverage and the public moved on.
More recently, the hacker reappeared with a more appealing proposal: they would drop the apparent files free of charge. "The torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects," Cyberleek said on their website.
Polygon cannot confirm the veracity of these files; Rockstar Games and Xbox did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Yet even as some hoaxes related to Cyberleek seem likely, the larger claim about the game files appears to be legitimate. Since Cyberleek dropped the alleged executable, savvy GTA 6 fans gathering on Discord have shared steady progress on making the game accessible on Linux, Mac, and Windows PC. These initial attempts don't seem impressive, especially when the game barely functions, stutters, or displays rudimentary graphics without textures and lighting .
It would be a mistake to dismiss the reverse engineering projects though. The first big hurdle — getting the game to run at all — has already been overcome​​​​​​​ . A few hours after entering the game for the first time, hackers managed​​​​​​​ to load some of GTA 6 's shaders, which help the game get closer to its full visual fidelity.
Under normal circumstances, before artificial-intelligence coding assistance became readily available ,​​​​​​​ incremental progress like this could have taken years for a game as complex as GTA 6 . To be sure, it may still be weeks, if not months, before​​​​​​​ an unauthorized PC port of GTA 6 seems plausible. Given the enormous interest in the game — and the PC gaming community feeling slighted​​​​​​​ for being left out — a port may just be a matter of time. If it comes to pass, fans may also be able to access the game without paying for it.​​​​​​​

articles.txt:
Unofficial GTA 6 PC projects have begun rendering parts of the game world, with VIctory reaching the first mission sequence but suffering severe graphical and performance problems. Separate footage shows partially working shaders and models. No verified, fully playable public PC build exists, and major development challenges remain.

Unofficial GTA 6 PC compatibility projects have reportedly moved beyond initial in-game menus, with newly shared footage showing early 3D environments and partially functioning shaders. This development comes just a day after the missing executable from the leaked Xbox Series X|S build surfaced online.
As we previously reported , developers managed to boot GTA 6 on PC within three hours of the executable's release. At the time, progress was limited to the game's initial settings and legal screens, with no actual playable areas.
Popular Now: GTA 6 boots on PC only 3 hours after Xbox executable leaked Now, multiple Xbox-to-PC compatibility projects are making progress toward rendering the game's 3D environments, with portions of the development process reportedly being streamed live on Discord.
One of these projects, called VIctory , is an open-source compatibility layer designed to execute GTA 6's original Xbox x86-64 code directly on Windows while reimplementing console-specific functionality and translating GPU shaders.
3 VIctory is an open-source compatibility layer for running the Xbox Series X|S build of GTA 6 on Windows; the project reports reaching the first mission’s intro, but most of the scene still fails to render. (Image: Github) VIEW GALLERY - 3 IMAGES According to the project's November 23 development update, testing on a Windows 11 system equipped with an AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT has demonstrated 30 FPS in the menus, working save functionality, and intro video playback with audio. The project also loads into the game world in about 50 seconds, reaching the first mission's introductory sequence.
However, rendering remains severely limited, with most of the scene missing and individual frames taking between 0.5 and 1.8 seconds to render, equivalent to approximately 0.6 - 2 FPS. Entering the game world can also cause GPU hangs and display driver resets.
Interestingly, Reddit user u/bingusmakesbread has shared footage purportedly showing further progress, including partially functioning shaders, character models, and environmental rendering.
The user clarified that the footage originates from a separate private project that could eventually be integrated into one of the existing public projects or released independently.
The architectural similarities between Microsoft's Xbox Series consoles and modern Windows PCs help explain the rapid progress. Rather than emulating an entirely different CPU architecture, developers can focus on translating console-specific graphics functionality and implementing the necessary system services.
There is also a significant obstacle regarding game ownership and distribution. Even so, Xbox Series X|S owners running up-to-date firmware reportedly have no straightforward way to extract their own decrypted copy of GTA 6 for use with these projects.
There's a live tracker called Portwatch that monitors projects that recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox Series build to PC. At the time of writing, VIctory sits at 67% completion; note this scale is not linear: 55% is reached at the main menu, 70% when in-game, 85% at 30 FPS, and 100% when stable. The last stretch will likely need much more development time, effort, and AI tokens.
3 Portwatch puts the leading unofficial GTA 6 PC project at 72% on its progress scale, past the in-game milestone but short of the 30 FPS mark. (Image: Portwatch) Story Q&A Powered by TweakBot

articles.t: En France, GTA 6 a été le 2e meilleur lancement d’un jeu physique de l’histoire
GTA 6 Online cultive autant de questions que de promesses
articles.chapeau: Le plus gros défi de Rockstar ?
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto VI est encore loin d'avoir révélé tous ses secrets aux dizaines de millions de joueurs qui s'y adonnent chaque jour depuis le 19 novembre, mais déjà la question se pose : que doit faire Rockstar Games avec Grand Theft Auto Online ? Une question simple en apparence mais qui reste enveloppée d'un épais mystère et qui divise la communauté.
Au risque d'enfoncer des portes ouvertes, si Grand Theft Auto V s'est écoulé à 235 millions d'exemplaires au fil des générations, ce n'est pas uniquement pour les beaux yeux de Michael, Trevor et Franklin. Le secret (de polichinelle) de la longévité de GTA 5 est à chercher du côté de Grand Theft Auto Online , un univers si endurant et si populaire que Rockstar a même fini par lui adjoindre un abonnement GTA+ pour gratter toujours plus d'argent et générer toujours plus d'engagement.
GTA Online , c'est gros comment, déjà ? Selon les données exposées publiquement en avril 2026 à la suite d'une intrusion revendiquée par le collectif ShinyHunters, les joueurs ont dépensé plus de 5 milliards de dollars dans GTA Online entre 2014 et 2024, sachant que l'année 2020 a constitué un pic de popularité avec 744 millions de dollars. Selon la fuite, les recettes annuelles de GTA Online ne sont jamais descendues sous la barre des 400 millions de dollars depuis 2017, l'année du grand décollage avec 504 millions de dollars. Sur la période allant de septembre 2025 à avril 2026, environ 74 % des dépenses provenaient des Shark Cards et 26 % de l'abonnement GTA+.
Ces fortunes, les joueurs les dépensent pour débloquer plus rapidement des véhicules et les customiser, mais aussi des armes, tenues et accessoires pour leur avatar, sans oublier des appartements de luxe, des yachts, des boîtes de nuit ou d'autres lieux de production permettant de débloquer des activités et des revenus passifs. Et pour maintenir l'engagement, la culture du grind ainsi que la frustration de n'avoir jamais assez d'argent, GTA Online pratique naturellement des prix prohibitifs qui poussent à emprunter le chemin le plus court et le plus cher.
Initialement considéré (à tort) comme un simple mode multijoueur intégré à GTA V , ne serait-ce que parce qu'il était conditionné à l'achat de ce dernier, GTA Online a évolué au point de devenir un jeu à part entière, que l'on peut se procurer séparément depuis qu'il a fait son apparition sur PS5 et Xbox Series, le 15 mars 2022. Durant toutes ces années, Rockstar Games n'a cessé de muscler sa proposition, en commençant par l'arrivée des braquages à quatre joueurs en 2015.
En ajoutant toujours plus de façons de faire fortune, GTA Online a aussi connu une évolution dans sa tonalité. D'abord ancré dans le réalisme habituel de la franchise, le jeu est devenu plus fantaisiste, chaotique et parfois absurde. Le tournant est souvent attribué au « braquage de la fin du monde », la grande mise à jour de décembre 2017. À partir de là, les joueurs ont commencé à voir arriver des motos volantes, des véhicules extraterrestres et d'autres éléments tout droit sortis de Saints Row . Vous vous en doutez, une bonne partie de la communauté n'a pas apprécié cette orientation et on pourrait même dire que GTA Roleplay (on va en parler) est monté en puissance en réponse à l'escalade militaro-futuriste de GTA Online .
Il est important de rappeler quelque chose de basique : officiellement, GTA 6 Online n'existe pas. À ce jour, Rockstar Games n'a rien laissé paraître, ni teasé , ni rien du tout. Il y a bien des portions de la carte de GTA 6 que Jason et Lucia ne visitent jamais, ni durant la quête principale ni dans les missions optionnelles, dont un zoo, un cimetière, deux casinos et une petite ville au nord. Sur ce point, Stephen Donkin, le vice-président du design, a confirmé au site Kotaku que Rockstar Games en a gardé sous la pédale : « La carte a été conçue sur le long terme et en tenant compte de nombreux facteurs. Il y a donc quelques zones sur la carte qui nous offrent des options pour l'avenir, au cas où nous en aurions besoin pour le gameplay ou la narration ». Il y a plusieurs interprétations possibles, l'une étant que ces commentaires font référence à du futur contenu additionnel solo. Et si ces préparatifs concernent bel et bien le jeu en ligne, eh bien tant mieux, ça veut dire qu'il ne faudra pas attendre six ans avant l'ouverture du casino, qui n'était arrivé qu'en 2019 dans GTA Online .
Mais avant d'imaginer quels genres de contenus et de fonctionnalités nous attendent dans ce GTA 6 Online

articles.txt:
Add preferred source GTA 6 set an all-time record for the biggest first-day launch in entertainment history, generating $3.79 billion (~5.1 trillion won) in worldwide retail sales on its opening day. Pre-orders of 32.5 million copies and a Metacritic score of 99 had signaled the record run well before release. But less than a week after launch, attempts were detected to run a hacked, leaked Xbox executable file on PC by modifying it with Claude AI. A developer group called "Project Leonida" has begun work on a port, with projections that it could reach a playable state within about a week. Rockstar Games has typically released PC versions about a year after console versions, but observers suggest this incident could push the PC release forward to the first quarter of next year. Key Elements GTA 6 Rockstar Games Cyberleek Project Leonida Claude AI Eurogamer PlayStation 5 Xbox Series X|S GTA 5 The crime action game "Grand Theft Auto (GTA) 6" generated $3.79 billion (~5.1 trillion won) in retail sales on its first day, setting an all-time record for the biggest opening day in entertainment industry history. But less than a week after release, attempts have been detected to run a hacked, leaked executable file on PC by modifying it with artificial intelligence (AI), fueling speculation that the spread of an unofficial PC version could prompt an earlier official PC release.
Rockstar Games said in an official announcement on the 20th (local time) that GTA 6 had racked up $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales by the close of its launch day on the 19th. The company described it as the biggest first-day performance ever across all media, including games, film and music. That far surpasses the $800 million (~1.1 trillion won) first-day sales and $1 billion (~1.3 trillion won) three-day cumulative total of its predecessor "GTA 5," released in September 2013. GTA 6 pulled in roughly 4.7 times its predecessor's first-day figure in a single day, instantly eclipsing the record the earlier title set over three days.
Signs of the blockbuster performance were evident before launch. Pre-orders hit 32.5 million copies, a record across all platforms, and the game scored 99 out of 100 from critics on the global game review site Metacritic. The game, the first proper sequel in 13 years, is set in the fictional state of Leonida and Vice City, modeled on the United States, and follows protagonists Jason and Lucia as they become entangled in criminal cases. The series' previous installment, GTA 5, has sold about 235 million copies cumulatively, with the franchise as a whole having sold about 480 million copies.
Records also tumbled in music. The official soundtrack "GTA 6: The Album," produced by Rockstar Games in collaboration with the record label Atlantic Records, features 34 tracks with contributions from Blackpink's Jennie, Dua Lipa, Lana Del Rey, Playboi Carti and others. It logged about 29.85 million Spotify streams on its first day, setting an all-time first-day streaming record for a game soundtrack album, and three pre-released tracks each entered the top 10 of the Billboard charts.
The trouble surfaced right after those blockbuster figures were confirmed. According to the British gaming outlet Eurogamer, an anonymous hacker known as "Cyberleek," who breached Rockstar Games in August and stole its entire development files, recently released the executable file for GTA 6's Xbox version publicly. articles.chapeau: Project Leonida lost its GitHub page and its Discord was reportedly taken down after the GTA 6 Xbox leak. No GTA 6 PC port is playable yet, either.
articles.txt:
The GTA 6 Xbox leak hasn’t yielded a playable PC port, and Rockstar hasn’t confirmed whether it requested the removal of Project Leonida’s Discord server.
0:00 Unofficial GTA 6 PC port projects are going offline days after a leaked Xbox build was released.
None of the projects has made GTA 6 playable on PC. Project Leonida, which aimed to get the Xbox Series X build running on PC, lost its GitHub page. VGC reports a claim that Leonida’s Discord server was taken down at the request of Rockstar and its parent company, Take-Two.
The server had around 179,000 members, with 74,000 online. There’s no evidence of emails from Rockstar or Discord, and Rockstar and Take-Two have said nothing.
On 18 November, Take-Two used DMCA takedowns against unofficial GTA 5 ports on GitHub. In August, it subpoenaed Discord for data on Cyberleek, the account behind the GTA 6 leak. Rockstar’s modding guidelines also restrict unofficial ports.
Leonida’s GitHub page returned a 404 error, not a DMCA notice. The error points more towards the project’s operators having deleted the page, but it doesn’t prove they did.
Cyberleek released the Xbox build on 19 November without the executable, promising to release it sooner if a meme coin reached a $15 million target. The coin missed that target, but Cyberleek released the executable the following Monday anyway. According to Decrypt, the GTA6Modding Discord server was removed the next day, and other groups, including Chasm, locked down their servers.
Many projects are using AI chatbots such as Claude to write their code. Two projects, VIctory and XCL, can load the game world, but neither can run it in a playable state. Don’t download anything advertised as GTA 6 for PC; some carry infostealers.

articles.t: Benchmark finds GTA 6 PS5 performance inferior to Xbox Series X, with more framerate drops
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 on the Xbox Series X has fewer performance drawbacks than on the base PS5. Digital Foundry discovered that framerates stay closer to the 30 fps target on the Microsoft system. VRR at 120Hz also helps the Series X maintain smoother graphics in congested Leonida scenes.
articles.txt:
A new benchmark shows how the GTA 6 Xbox Series X version outshines the base PS5 alternative . Digital Foundry compared performance on the rival consoles. While the differences aren’t enormous, the Rockstar title exhibited more infrequent framerate drops on Microsoft’s hardware.
Image quality is very similar on the Series X and the most affordable PlayStation . Both platforms support features like ray-traced global illumination and reflections. At 30 fps , the native 1440p resolution upscales to 4K, with temporal anti-aliasing (TAA) smoothing out jagged edges. Digital Foundry observed only minor variations in how effects like heat haze render.
The two consoles begin to diverge during fast-action gameplay , driving , or crowded Leonida environments . When Lucia races through a packed airport, framerates fall into the mid to upper 20s. Explosions worsen the stuttering, pushing readings closer to 20 fps. The GTA 6 PS5 version fares slightly worse in the most demanding scenes.
Framerates are more stable on GTA 6 Xbox benchmarks. Still, VRR at 120Hz produces the biggest disparity. On compatible displays, Microsoft’s system employs low framerate compensation (LFC) at below 48 fps. The base PlayStation doesn’t have that capability, making performance seem inconsistent.
The site calls the results “surprising,” but the Rockstar project is a unique case. Pushing hardware to its limits, the marginally superior Series X GPU benefits. Although the PS5 chip runs at a higher clock speed, it has 44% fewer compute units.
Amplifying demand for a PC port , no console achieves greater than 30 fps. Regardless, Digital Foundry confirmed GTA 6 on the PS5 Pro is the best existing option. Aided by PSSR 2 upscaling , the 4K output looks noticeably crisper. Meanwhile, ray-traced shadows make already realistic scenery more lifelike. Framerates are steadier, rarely dipping under its target.
For budget-conscious gamers, the Xbox Series S may introduce fewer performance compromises than expected. Unique to the console, FSR 4.1 boosts the native 720p resolution to a respectable 1080p. Even so, lower-quality shadows are apparent, along with audio drops that updates have not yet addressed.

articles.txt:
In 2022, Rockstar Games went into a panic when a major Grand Theft Auto VI leak appeared online. The most anticipated game in history became a hot topic on social media and forums after its first images and details were revealed.
Some time later, the person responsible was caught: Arion Kurtaj. His story became notorious because, at just 17 years old, he managed to compromise the security systems of Rockstar, Revolut, Uber, and other companies using nothing more than a smartphone and an Amazon Fire TV Stick.
His hacking spree came to an end with his arrest, confinement in a psychiatric facility, and the sentence he received after pleading guilty.
The moment of truth arrived for Arion Kurtaj, now 21, before the judge overseeing his case at Woolwich Crown Court. It’s worth remembering that, days before the game’s release, the young man pleaded guilty in an attempt to avoid prison.
Although the possibility of spending years behind bars was real, a BBC report revealed that the authorities showed leniency toward the young hacker, who was part of the Lapsus$ group.
The judge determined that the time Arion Kurtaj had spent in pretrial detention and subsequently in a psychiatric institution had been sufficient in terms of confinement and restrictions on his social life.
As a result, he was sentenced to conditional release under a Serious Crime Prevention Order that will remain in effect for 5 years. During this period, the young hacker will not be allowed to engage in online activities or use platforms such as Telegram and Discord.
Arion Kurtaj, the hacker who brought Rockstar Games to its knees in 2022.
The proceedings established that Arion Kurtaj had committed a crime, which is why he was held in custody while awaiting the outcome of his case and the corresponding sentence.
However, the unusual circumstances surrounding his actions surprised the authorities. The young man managed to cause major problems for important companies using everyday devices such as a smartphone and an Amazon Fire Stick from a hotel.
That’s why the judge who sentenced him praised his abilities, while also expressing hope that he would use his talent for good and never reoffend:
“You are a very talented young man. Don’t let this happen again.”
Four years ago, Rockstar Games said it was disappointed by the leak, particularly because it revealed an important detail about GTA 6: the game would feature a female protagonist, whom we now know to be Lucia Caminos.

articles.t: GTA 6 EXE Leak: 57 MB File, 0 Playable PC Builds
articles.chapeau: CyberLeek released a 57 MB GTA 6 executable for Xbox build 1.0.2.1. It does not run the game, and Project Leonida has no playable PC build.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games CyberLeek, the group behind the alleged Grand Theft Auto 6 Xbox dump, released a 57 MB executable on November 23, 2026, and modders have already started picking at it, according to LevelUp’s report on the GTA 6 executable leak . The headline sounds like a finish line. It is closer to a starting gun.
The file comes from an Xbox Series X|S build, not from any official PC release, and a CyberLeek administrator has already said in plain terms that it does not run the game. This article sorts what outlets have actually reported from what forum threads and social posts are promising. It follows our earlier piece on the five CyberLeek claims and the one missing file , which flagged exactly this gap.
Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
Here is the short version. Reports say CyberLeek published the executable tied to the leaked Xbox build on November 23, 2026. That executable reportedly matches version 1.0.2.1 of the Xbox Series X|S build, and the archive that carries it weighs 57 MB.
The leak does not stand alone. An earlier alleged dump of the same build circulated as a 209 GB torrent. Per the reporting, that torrent held files for Rockstar’s RAGE game engine and for the Xbox console. What it lacked was the executable, the small program that ties those files together and tells the hardware what to do with them.
Coverage has come from several named outlets. LevelUp, eTeknix, ShiftDelete.Net and TechJuice all ran the story, and the outlets we can link to directly include GamesIndustry.biz, which framed it as a leaker reportedly releasing the file needed to run the leaked Xbox build . The word “reportedly” appears in that headline for a reason. Nobody outside the leak community has confirmed that the files are authentic or complete.
The core point for readers is simple. A leaked executable does not equal a playable game. It is one missing piece in a pile that still has plenty of missing pieces.
Size comparisons make this story look lopsided. The archive is 57 MB, while the earlier alleged dump ran to 209 GB. Yet the small file is the one that modders had been waiting for. We said as much when the dump first surfaced, in our look at how PC port hopes hinged on one missing file in 209 GB .
Think of the dump as a warehouse of parts and the executable as the assembly instructions. Game assets, engine files and console components tell you what the game contains. The executable tells you how the pieces connect and what code runs when the game starts. Without it, a port team can study the parts but cannot easily see how the machine fits together.
That explains why outlets treated the release as a development worth reporting. PCMag had earlier covered the saga under the headline GTA 6 leaker releases all files for alleged Xbox build of game , and the new archive extends that story rather than replacing it.
It also explains why the number 57 matters less than the version label. Version 1.0.2.1 gives modders a fixed target. When a community works from one specific build, people can compare notes, share findings and avoid chasing mismatched files. That coordination is often what turns a scattered hobby into a real project.
The most important sentence in this story came from CyberLeek itself. Coverage of the release quotes an unnamed CyberLeek administrator as writing: “This .exe file does NOT RUN THE GAME.” That is about as direct as a leaker gets.
The same administrator reportedly set expectations on timing too. The reported line reads: “It will take at least a week for us to get somewhere noticeable to the point where you can play on your pc.” Two details stand out. The group says “at least,” which makes a week a floor and not a promise. And “noticeable” is a modest target, well short of “finished” or even “stable.”
Some social posts have run ahead of that. One claim says a playable PC version will arrive within days. Reports do not confirm it, and it conflicts with the administrator’s own estimate. Another claim says modders have already built a playable PC version. The reporting says the opposite, describing a build that stays unplayable or only partly boots.
Why does a console executable not simply run on a Windows machine? Because it was compiled for different hardware, different system libraries and a different operating environment. The code expects an Xbox to be underneath it. A PC is not an X

articles.t: GTA VI: Cyberleek is distributing the game’s executable file!
Unofficial GTA 6 PC port effort suffers setback as Rockstar seemingly takes down Project Leonida, one of the internet's biggest recompilation projects
articles.chapeau: Mere hours after Project Leonida modders managed to get Grand Theft Auto 6 running on PC, Rockstar has seemingly stepped in to shut it down.
articles.txt:
A lot has happened in the last 24 hours in the community working to get Grand Theft Auto 6 running on PC. And now, Rockstar has dealt a major blow to their efforts.
After infamous leaker CyberLeek made good on their promise and released a full Xbox build of GTA 6 , the build immediately spread online amongst modders and recompilers. Their goal? Get the game playable on PC as soon as possible.
The largest hub of all that activity has been the Project Leonida Discord server, which had its own repository and a team of volunteer modders working - with help from Claude AI - to recompile GTA 6's leaked Xbox build to run on PC. Rockstar has allegedly taken down the server, causing the project's leaders to dismantle the entire operation.
Project Leonida's lead NotRexed posted on X to announce they're ending development, after fans noticed the Discord server has been removed, as has Project Leonida's GitHub repository .
"I quit guys. I'm sorry," NotRexed wrote. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can't control so I'm stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity."
The modder, who claims to be a "15 year-old kid", later wrote in a follow-up X post that Rockstar is behind the server's takedown, though that's not the only reason for the project's end.
"Last post from me. I wanna clear things up," they wrote. "Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I've said before, I'm a 15 year-old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye."
Before the Project Leonida server disappeared, footage emerged showing GTA 6 running on PC . The game is able to reach the initial setup screen, but quickly goes into a black screen afterwards. As unimpressive as the result was, it was achieved within hours of the full Xbox build's leak.
Incidentally, while Project Leonida was the biggest and most prominent of the various GTA 6 recompilation projects, the leaking of the full Xbox build has given rise to various other groups. PortWatch VI is a website dedicated to tracking their progress, and though the data is almost entirely self-reported, a few other teams appear to have made notable progress themselves, so this may not be the end of the story.
Rockstar has yet to comment publicly on the Xbox build's leak, and the company has not announced GTA 6 for PC. However, a report suggested GTA 6 arrives on PC in the first quarter of 2027 , earlier than everyone expected.

articles.t: GTA VI sur PC : le portage non officiel CGBJ lance déjà le jeu
articles.chapeau: Après la fuite de l'exécutable, cinq portages non officiels de GTA VI avancent sur PC. CGBJ atteint déjà le jeu, sans éclairage, et reste privé.
articles.txt:
Il n'aura pas fallu plus de vingt-quatre heures. Depuis que CyberLeek a publié lundi 23 novembre l'exécutable de la build Xbox Series de GTA VI , plusieurs portages PC non officiels ont réussi à faire démarrer le jeu. Et selon DSOGaming , l'un d'eux, baptisé CGBJ , atteint déjà les phases de jeu, alors que Leonida , le projet le plus attendu, a jeté l'éponge dans la nuit.
Le site recense cinq émulateurs ou portages majeurs : CGBJ , VIctory , XCL , Xbox2Windows et TuxBox . Les deux derniers parviennent à lancer GTA VI et à afficher sa première image. XCL et VIctory vont plus loin, jusqu'au menu principal, et faisaient figure de favoris avant l'apparition de CGBJ.
Les deux projets ne s'y prennent pas tout à fait comme Leonida, qui misait sur la recompilation statique du code du jeu . XCL , écrit en Rust et publié sous licence GPL-2.0 le 20 novembre, se présente comme une couche de compatibilité entre la Xbox Series et Windows, dans l'esprit de Wine ou de Proton . Il n'émule pas le processeur : le code x64 du jeu tourne directement sur le PC, tandis que XCL réécrit de son côté les bibliothèques système de la console, comme kernelx.dll ou d3d12_xs.dll, et recompile les shaders RDNA2 de la console en shaders PC. Son dépôt affirme faire déjà tourner entièrement Minecraft Preview , Unicorn Overlord , Fortnite et XDefiant , dans la limite de leurs services en ligne.
VIctory , lui aussi écrit en Rust, sous licence GPL-3.0, est né dans la soirée du 23 novembre avec un seul objectif : faire tourner GTA VI sur Windows à partir des fichiers fournis par l'utilisateur. Son état des lieux est précis : le jeu démarre, affiche ses écrans de premier lancement, sa vidéo d'introduction avec le son et ses menus à 30 images par seconde, puis charge le monde en une cinquantaine de secondes. Mais une fois dans la première mission, seul le titre s'affiche, la scène reste sombre et chaque image prend de 0,5 à 1,8 seconde. Une partie des shaders n'est pas encore traduite, et le projet prévient que l'entrée dans le monde peut figer la carte graphique au point de forcer Windows à relancer son pilote. Les deux dépôts cumulent déjà plusieurs milliers d'étoiles sur GitHub.
CGBJ est une version privée de VIctory qui reprend une partie des travaux de XCL. D'après DSOGaming, sa dernière version permet de se déplacer à la manette, de parler aux personnages non joueurs et d'ouvrir le menu du jeu. Un résultat obtenu en moins de vingt-quatre heures, qui reste très loin d'une version jouable : il n'y a pas d'éclairage et les performances sont mauvaises. John Papadopoulos , qui s'attendait à voir Leonida arriver le premier à ce stade, juge toutefois ces images légitimes, contrairement aux fausses vidéos qui montraient le jeu tourner avec de superbes graphismes.
Il appelle malgré tout à la prudence : les images semblent authentiques et PortWatch les aurait confirmées, mais elles pourraient encore être fausses. Derrière CGBJ, XCL et VIctory plantent pour l'instant au moment d'entrer dans le jeu, mais ce n'est peut-être qu'une question d'heures avant qu'ils ne franchissent eux aussi cette étape. La prochaine sera d'afficher des images correctes, sans artefacts, avant de s'attaquer aux performances.
Les progrès s'enchaînent en effet. Sur X, le compte itsawful911 a publié mardi matin une nouvelle vidéo en assurant que les shaders commencent à fonctionner et que les cheveux des personnages s'affichent nettement mieux. Il se risquait même à prédire des visuels « presque parfaits » d'ici la fin de la journée, avant de passer à l'optimisation.
Pour les joueurs, ces avancées ne changent presque rien. CGBJ est un projet privé, impossible à télécharger, et ni XCL ni VIctory ne proposent de version publique. Leur code source est bien accessible sur GitHub et peut être compilé, mais il ne fournit aucun fichier du jeu : il suppose de disposer de la build qui a fuité, ce qui n'a rien de légal. Toute archive présentée comme un GTA VI prêt à installer est donc à fuir, d'autant que de faux portages truffés de logiciels malveillants circulent depuis des mois.
Ces projets avancent par ailleurs sous la menace de Take-Two , qui avait déjà multiplié les demandes de retrait depuis la diffusion de la build par CyberLeek . Rockstar n'a toujours annoncé aucune version PC officielle, qu'un rapport paru en octobre situait au premier trimestre 2027. D'ici là, la course entre les portages non officiels promet de se jouer à l'heure près.

articles.t: GTA 6 PC Ports ‘Nuked’ Just Days Before Devs Expected It to Be Playable
Hackers leak GTA 6 Xbox file, fueling PC speculation
Leaker Cyberleek Releases The Xbox Build Executable for GTA 6
articles.chapeau: Not even a month into the GTA 6 glory, the leaker publishes the complete .exe file as an "early Christmas present."
articles.txt:
Not even a month into the GTA 6 glory, the leaker publishes the complete .exe file as an "early Christmas present."
Less than a week after GTA 6, which had been in production for over a decade, finally had its moment as " the biggest entertainment launch in history across all industries ," an infamous leaker made its full build public. Cyberleek posted the Xbox build executable online, just as promised .
Originally, Cyberleek only posted a near-complete GTA 6 build without the .exe. The missing precious executable was the very piece of the puzzle tying everything together and making it possible to run the build. The leaker stated that the full file would be out once their crypto coin hit the $15 million market cap. Otherwise, they would just give it out on November 23 – whichever happens first. The bold $15-million financial goal was out of reach, so the leaker released the file on November 23 as an "early Christmas present."
In the "release note," Cyberleek also commented on Take-Two Interactive's ongoing efforts to track them down.
"Months of takedowns, subpoenas, and wallet tracing later, the hunt is still on, and the uploads keep arriving. No budget makes a lock unbreakable, and no court order deletes what the internet already has," the cocky statement from the leaker reads.
This leak paves the way for developers to create a fully playable PC build way before Rockstar even announces one. However, since creating a full-scale version of the game in a short period of time is unrealistic, the first PC version of GTA 6 will very likely be an AI-made emulation of the game.
Although many players are excited to see the free .exe file just a few days into the launch, other users are not as blindly optimistic about the leak. Considering how quickly and unapologetically the industry shifted from physical copies to digital downloads as a more profitable distribution model, the Cyberleek situation might be the perfect excuse for publishers to give up on the concept of players owning a game entirely.
"My only worry is that the Cyberleek issue will be the prime example publishers will point to in the future when games are no longer downloaded but rather streamed completely. I'm not looking forward to that," a Reddit user wrote.
With this in mind, whether what Cyberleek is doing is ethical or not is a big question. "CYBERLEEK is about fighting anti-consumerism in the games industry. It was never about damaging the players," the leaker's note says. However, no matter their intentions, these leaks might eventually harm the players. The "billion-dollar companies" Cyberleek refers to are still doing fine after the leaks, but the way they approach game distribution might change, and players will be the ones affected by it.

Their goal isn't necessarily to get rich and buy flashy cars or a mansion, but so they can lay the foundation for their family. The group (or individual) responsible for the leak, Cyberleek, had said the release of the executable (EXE) — which was the missing piece of the previously leaked full build — would come on November 23, and they made good on that promise .
Or at least that's what has been widely reported , and there's plenty of evidence to suggest it's true — including some footage of the rapid progress made by those attempting to create a playable PC version (which, in case of any doubt, are obviously efforts that are illegal).

The reason work is so speedy is because it's being vastly accelerated by the modders involved using AI to reverse engineer the leaked Xbox code in order to produce a PC version of GTA 6 . There are two ways to do that — either a working copy that runs via emulation on PC, or a recompilation of the leaked Xbox code that actually runs natively.

articles.chapeau: Après la fuite de l'exécutable, GTA VI démarre sur PC, vidéo à l'appui. Mais le projet Leonida a disparu dans la nuit, et ses copies prennent le relais.
articles.txt:
C'était la pièce manquante. Depuis le 19 novembre, une archive de 209 Go présentée comme la build Xbox 1.0.2.1 de GTA VI circulait par torrent, mise en ligne par CyberLeek sans son exécutable principal, le fichier qui contient tout le code du jeu. Le fichier est accompagné d'empreintes SHA-256 permettant de vérifier les téléchargements, ce qui ne garantit pas pour autant qu'il provienne de Rockstar Games . Ni l'éditeur ni sa maison mère Take-Two n'avaient encore réagi en fin de journée.
« L'exe est sorti. Toujours gratuit. Un cadeau de Noël en avance de la part de CL. Le flambeau passe aux projets open source de recompilation et d'émulation. »
Le leaker n'en continue pas moins de solliciter des dons pour un mystérieux projet « pour les joueurs ». Dans le fichier d'accompagnement de la build, il assure que « personne n'est obligé de donner quoi que ce soit » et que chaque publication restera gratuite, tout en présentant chaque don comme « un vote pour davantage de ceci », au même titre que chaque échange de son jeton.
L'exécutable ne serait pas chiffré, et c'est ce qui change tout pour Leonida , le projet de recompilation statique dont nous détaillions le fonctionnement et l'avancée il y a deux jours. Son auteur, ItsNotRexed , déjà à l'origine de Hookshot, le portage PC du remake de Zelda Ocarina of Time , assurait que tout ce qui pouvait être fait sans ce fichier était prêt. Selon Numerama , les développeurs l'ont chargé dans leur outil moins d'une heure après sa publication.
Sur la machine d'un contributeur, avec des correctifs pas encore intégrés au projet, le jeu passe déjà une douzaine d'étapes de son démarrage : il réserve sa mémoire, crée son périphérique graphique et plus de 500 listes de commandes, soit environ 1 200 appels graphiques. Il se bloque ensuite sur la gestion de la mémoire graphique, l'un des points où la Xbox et le PC diffèrent le plus. Autrement dit, le code du jeu tournait bel et bien sur PC, sans encore rien afficher.
La situation a évolué en quelques heures. Selon Eurogamer , les membres du serveur Discord de Leonida , devenu le point de ralliement de tous les efforts de recompilation de GTA VI , ont publié une vidéo du jeu qui démarre sur PC : on le voit aller jusqu'aux réglages initiaux, avant de tomber sur un écran noir. Les moddeurs auraient obtenu ce résultat avec l'aide de l'intelligence artificielle Claude . Le site précise toutefois ne pas avoir pu vérifier directement ces affirmations, et la build n'est clairement pas jouable en l'état.
Un message publié dans la soirée sur le Discord du projet, repéré par GamesRadar , résumait la situation : le jeu « démarre presque », avec un écran noir et un son qui se coupe. Cet écran noir signifie que la couche graphique, chargée de convertir les appels DirectX de la Xbox en appels Vulkan, ne fonctionne pas encore. À force d'obstination, des contributeurs sont tout de même parvenus jusqu'à l'écran de chargement du jeu.
Pour la suite, Shayder , l'un des principaux développeurs du projet, a prévenu dans un message publié puis supprimé sur X qu'il fallait « s'attendre à beaucoup de travail de recompilation statique très bientôt ». Sur le Discord de Leonida , il a ensuite estimé qu'il faudrait environ une semaine pour que le jeu devienne jouable sur PC. Une échéance que la nuit suivante a rendue bien incertaine.
Le projet n'aura pas tenu la nuit. Lundi soir, Leonida a d'abord déménagé vers une nouvelle organisation GitHub, puis tout s'est arrêté, raconte Numerama : vers minuit, son serveur Discord, qui comptait près de 179 000 membres, ne répondait plus, et vers une heure du matin, le dépôt GitHub, suivi par plus de 33 000 personnes, avait disparu. articles.t: "The torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects": GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek claims to have released crimsim's Xbox executable and denies crypto grifting
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek has claimed to have released the executable file for an Xbox build of the game.
articles.txt:
GTA 6 leaker or leakers Cyberleek claim to to have released the main executable file for an alleged Xbox build of the game that they asserted they'd lobbed onto the net last week. In a fresh statement, the leakers alluded to the excutable being used in attempts to create an unofficial PC port of the crimsim, and denied that their use of cryptocurrency is just a grift.
Referring to the alleged executable as "an early Christmas gift", Cyberleek declared in the statement posted to their website that "the torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects". As of writing, the legitimacy of the executable doesn't appear to have been independently verified, meaning it could still just turn out to be a pile of malware or something similarly dodgy. Needless to say, given that and the fact software piracy is illegal, not touching it - or any of the other files Cyberleek claim to have posted - with a barge pole is the sensible thing to do.
Cyberleek have been bigging up the idea that these files they've been releasing could result in GTA 6 running on PC sharpish, via a modified version cobbled together with generative AI . That might happen, but I'm seriously skeptical that if it were to, it wouldn't just be dodgy jankware than runs like piss, rather than anything that'd compare remotely well to an official PC port.
Thus far, it appears a group of would-be recompilers going by Project Leonida may have got the game to start booting on PC, but they since look to have disappeared and scrubbed their established online presence.
All of this again raises the question of whether the threat of any sort of bodged PC recreation coming out of this alleged executable release may lead Rockstar to narrow the gap between this month's console release and its eventual Windows release, which reports have previously claimed is planned for the opening months of next year.
Returning to Cyberleek's latest statement, the leaker or leakers have also taken the opportunity to insist that their attempts to pump up a crypto coin as part of the leaking is just for practical reasons rather than grifty ones , honest. "Every donation is a vote for more of this," they wrote. "Where the votes go, [Cyberleek] follows. Crypto here is just a tool - there is no other way to move funds without names."
Rockstar called the initial barrage of leaks laid claim to by Cyberleek "heartbreaking". Along with parent company Take-Two, they began a hunt for the identity of the leakers back in August, but that doesn't seem to to have deterred Cyberleek, if indeed the people leaking under the name are still the same ones as in the summer.
